rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a surface treatment (polishing/annealing) to homogenize Q235 steel microstructure, while the target paper deposits an AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating via APS and anneals it. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions—one is a surface modification of the base metal, the other is an applied coating.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at room temperature and ~70°C, whereas the target paper uses 3.5 wt% H2SO4 for electrochemical tests and 900°C cyclic hot corrosion with Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 salt mixtures. The environments and temperature regimes are completely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes microstructural homogenization leading to a uniform passive iron oxide film that suppresses pitting. The target paper's mechanism involves grain refinement, BCC phase strengthening, and formation of Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides from the HEA coating to resist corrosion and hot corrosion. These are different general classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower corrosion current, reduced mass loss, and less pitting in NaCl solution. The target paper predicts and reports higher microhardness, higher polarization resistance, lower corrosion current in H2SO4, and lower hot-corrosion weight gain at 900°C. The properties and test environments differ entirely.
